problem: LLMs trained on isolated KG head-relation-tail triples may not learn the surrounding context needed for multi-hop reasoning, and unreliable lower-hop facts compound through deeper reasoning chains.
method: Context-augmented KG supervision over disease-specific KGs (Gastroparesis, Diabetes) extracted with GraphMERT. Each primary triple is augmented with supporting triples from the same source text chunk (tracked via a path_idx chunk identifier) selected by SapBERT triple-embedding cosine similarity and thresholding, forming a context graph (CG). Qwen3-14B is SFT'd under two regimes (KG-grounded vs CG-grounded), then an LLM-judged, history-aware adaptive repair stage targets unresolved one-hop failures (failure categorization, targeted QA regeneration, regression tracking, quarantine review, validation-set refresh), and finally RL on lower-hop QA items is applied from repaired vs unrepaired checkpoints, with evaluation on 3-5-hop items.
key_assumptions: Supporting context for a triple can be identified by same-source-chunk co-occurrence plus triple-embedding similarity. [p. 8]
Unresolved one-hop failures are a good proxy for missing knowledge that should drive targeted repair. [p. 2, p. 6]
SFT learns format/imitation while RL improves generalization, motivating lower-hop RL for deeper-hop transfer. [p. 2]
Synthetically generated MCQ QA items with triple-grounded correctness filtering are adequate supervision and evaluation. [p. 30]
main_contribution: Proposes and empirically compares context-augmented (CG-grounded) vs standard KG-grounded supervision for LLM multi-hop QA, plus an LLM-judged adaptive repair pipeline applied before RL; reports that context augmentation improves multi-hop performance and that RL from repaired checkpoints gives larger, more stable gains.
datasets: Gastroparesis KG (GraphMERT-extracted; Table 1: 6,900 rows, 6,018 unique triples, 4,790 concepts, 20 relation types)
Diabetes KG (GraphMERT-extracted subset; Table 1: 6,000 rows, 5,954 unique triples, 4,397 concepts, 28 relation types)
Generated multiple-choice QA items spanning 1-hop to 5-hop reasoning
benchmarks: In-house disease-specific 1-5-hop MCQ benchmark (no standard public benchmark used)
baselines: Repaired SFT checkpoints vs unrepaired SFT checkpoints before RL
Full combined variant: context-augmented + repaired + RL
metrics: Multiple-choice answer accuracy (per hop depth, incl. 3-hop/4-hop/5-hop)
Robustness to option shuffling (average absolute change in accuracy)
results: Across both diseases context-augmented supervision consistently improves multi-hop performance over KG-only supervision; adaptive repair brings models to 100% accuracy on the cleaned retained one-hop validation sets; RL initialized from repaired SFT checkpoints yields larger and more stable gains than from unrepaired checkpoints; option shuffling changes accuracy by under one percentage point on average (p. 30). Exact per-hop numbers are in the paper's tables and were not extracted here.
limitations: QA datasets used for SFT, repair, RL, and evaluation are synthetically generated. [p. 30]
Validation on only two disease-specific KGs; standard multi-hop benchmarks not used. [p. 30]
Retained/cleaned validation sets are modified by the repair loop that is being evaluated (reaching 100% on the cleaned retained set), which risks selection artifacts.
future_work: Not fully extracted; the paper dedicates Section 6 to limitations and future extensions (synthetic-data and domain-generalization concerns). [p. 30]
code_availability: No code or data repository URL was found in the full text, and GitHub searches for the framework and for GraphMERT returned no matching repositories. Code availability: not stated in the paper.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: Effectively none at the level of idea formulation: this paper implements the same context-graph supervision, adaptive one-hop repair, and lower-hop RL with deeper-hop evaluation. The only conceptual space left for a distinct contribution is methodological rigor rather than mechanism: matched-token/matched-example controls to isolate context from supervision volume, an untouched held-out evaluation set that the repair loop cannot edit, seed-level significance, and generalization beyond two disease-specific KGs.
relation_to_idea.basis: Method overlap 1.0 because the paper's contribution bullet and Section 3.3 describe attaching same-source-chunk supporting triples to each primary triple (KG- vs CG-grounded supervision) exactly as the idea proposes, plus the same LLM-judged repair and lower-hop RL stages; evaluation overlap 0.9 because it also evaluates transfer to 3-5-hop queries, differing only in using generated domain MCQ items instead of the standard benchmarks the idea leaves open (Assumption 5).
